lines: Blank panel, 4HP, carrying the maker's logo in one of eight colour schemes
A rising edge here steps the panel on to the next of the eight logo designs, wrapping round after the last one
Burst generator: every trigger fires a run of up to eight pulses, with a stepping CV alongside them, and the spacing can be tightened or scattered as the run goes on
Fires a burst by hand, as though a trigger had arrived at the burst input
Sets the time between pulses, reaching 1 second at the top on an exponential scale; with a cable in clk the knob instead scales the clock interval by a power of two, an eighth to sixteen times
Sets how many pulses a burst fires, a whole number from 0 to 8
Shortens each gap by dividing it by this figure once for every pulse so far, 1 to 2; at 1 the pulses stay evenly spaced and at 2 each gap is half the one before
Scatters the pulses, shifting each gap at random either way by a fraction of itself, 0 for exact spacing and 1 for a gap anywhere between nothing and twice its length
Picks what the CV output does across the burst: even steps up, even steps down, two patterns alternating about zero, positive random, negative random, a random walk, or random between -5V and 5V
Sets what the burst output carries: a gate lasting half the current gap, or a 10ms trigger
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the repetition modulation input, which is added to the repetitions knob; at full travel 10V there adds eight pulses
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the time modulation input, which is added to the time knob; at full travel 10V there covers the knob's whole range
A rising edge starts a burst, restarting one that is already running
A clock here takes over the timing: each gap becomes the measured interval between ticks scaled by the time knob, from an eighth of that interval to sixteen times it
Adds to the repetitions knob through its attenuverter, 10V adding eight pulses at full travel
Adds to the time knob through its attenuverter; a cable in clk overrides this input entirely
Carries each pulse of the burst at 10V, either as a gate half the current gap long or as a 10ms trigger, depending on the switch
A 10ms trigger at 10V, fired on the last pulse of the burst
The stepping CV set by the mode knob, holding each step until the next pulse and dropping to 0V when the burst ends; in the rising mode it reaches 5V on the last pulse
reburst.notes: Clock mode drops the time CV: with a cable in clk the module recomputes the gap from the raw time knob and the clock interval, so the time attenuverter and the time input have no effect. The cv output is held only for the length of the current gap, which is why it falls to 0V at the end of a burst.

lines: Wavefolder: the input is amplified until it folds back on itself, up to six times, with an offset that makes the folding uneven; polyphonic, following the channel count of the input
Sets the gain applied to the signal before folding, 0 to 14, and the higher the gain the more times the signal folds back
Offsets the signal before folding, -1 to +1, so the folds fall unevenly either side of zero
Sets how many folding passes are applied, 2, 4 or 6; the alternative folding algorithm on the menu does its folding in one pass and ignores this switch
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the fold modulation input, which is added to the fold knob; at full travel each volt there adds one to the gain
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the symmetry modulation input, which is added to the symmetry knob; at full travel 5V there covers the knob's whole range
The signal to fold, read as ±5V and scaled to ±1 before the gain; a polyphonic cable is folded channel by channel
Adds to the fold knob through its attenuverter, and it tracks audio rate as well as CV
Adds to the symmetry knob through its attenuverter, and it tracks audio rate as well as CV
The folded signal, run through a tanh curve and scaled back to ±5V, with the channel count of the input
Menu — Alternative folding algorithm — folds in a single pass instead of repeated passes, which makes the stages switch do nothing and changes how the symmetry knob behaves
Note — the folding runs at four times the sample rate, and the resampling shifts the phase of the output slightly against the input
refold.notes: The stages switch is configured with a display multiplier of 2, so its three positions read 2, 4 and 6 on the panel and in the tooltip while the parameter itself runs 1 to 3.

lines: Four channel quantizer: each input is snapped to the notes switched on in the current scene, with sixteen scenes and octave transposition per channel
Selects which of the sixteen scenes is quantized to and edited by the note buttons, numbered 1 to 16
Switches that note in or out of the current scene, lighting blue while it is on; all four channels quantize to the same set of notes
Transposes that channel by whole octaves, -4 to +4, added to the octave input and clamped to four octaves either way
Selects the scene, 1.6 scenes per volt added to the scenes knob, so 10V covers all sixteen
Transposes every output in semitones, rounded from 1.2 semitones per volt so 10V gives an octave; it moves the quantized note rather than the scale, despite the panel printing root
Transposes every output in whole octaves, one octave per 2.5V, added to each channel's octave trimpot and clamped to four octaves either way
The pitch to quantize on that channel, in volts per octave; with nothing patched it takes whatever is at the first channel's input
The quantized pitch for that channel, in volts per octave, after the scene's notes and both transpositions
Menu — Quantization mode — takes a pitch Down to the nearest note switched on, Up to it, or to whichever of the two is Nearest; Down is the default
Menu — Load scales — reads all sixteen scenes back in from a JSON file
Menu — Save scales — writes all sixteen scenes out to a JSON file; the scenes are saved with the patch as well
Note — Every note is switched off in all sixteen scenes when the module is placed, and an empty scene passes plain semitones, so a note button has to be turned on before a scale is heard
rewin.notes: The maker's tooltip for input 1 reads semi, the panel prints root, and the code adds the rounded semitone shift after quantization. The octave and root inputs are read once and applied to all four channels.

lines: Six channel stereo mixer with a three band EQ, pan and two sends on every channel, stereo returns, and a master EQ and level
Sets the level of that channel, -60dB to 0dB, and it starts fully down
Switches that channel out of the mix and back, latching on each press and lighting its lamp while the channel is muted; a muted channel feeds the sends nothing either
Sets the low shelf of that channel, -20dB to +20dB, hinged at 125Hz
Sets the mid band of that channel, -12.5dB to +12.5dB, peaking at 1200Hz
Sets the high shelf of that channel, -15dB to +15dB, hinged at 1800Hz
Pans that channel from full left to full right by attenuating the far side, so the near side never rises above the level set for the channel
Sets how much of that channel goes to the send 1 outputs, silent at the bottom and unity at the top, taken after its EQ, pan and level
Sets how much of that channel goes to the send 2 outputs, silent at the bottom and unity at the top, taken after its EQ, pan and level
Sets the level at the L and R outputs, -60dB to 0dB, starting at -30dB, and it scales the return inputs along with the channels
Sets the low shelf of the master mix, -10dB to +10dB, hinged at 120Hz
Sets the mid band of the master mix, -7dB to +7dB, peaking at 1300Hz
Sets the high shelf of the master mix, -7dB to +7dB, hinged at 1700Hz
The audio input of that channel; a polyphonic cable is summed to a single signal
Scales the level of that channel, multiplying the gain set by the knob by the voltage divided by 10, so 10V leaves the level as set and 0V silences it; unpatched it counts as 10V
Adds to the pan knob of that channel, 5V moving it hard to one side, and the sum is clamped at the ends of the travel
The return for send 1, added to the matching side of the master mix after the master EQ and scaled by the master level
The return for send 2, added to the matching side of the master mix after the master EQ and scaled by the master level
Carries that side of the send 1 mix, each channel taken after its EQ, pan and level and scaled by its send 1 knob
Carries that side of the send 2 mix, each channel taken after its EQ, pan and level and scaled by its send 2 knob
Carries that side of the master mix, after the master EQ and level, with the returns added in
Note — every channel also passes a fixed high pass at 35Hz and a 5dB cut above 12kHz, and the master a 35Hz high pass and a 2dB cut; nothing in the module clips the output
Note — Every channel level knob comes up fully down and the master at -30dB, so nothing reaches the outputs until a channel is raised
rexmix.notes: The README quotes the channel EQ as ±12dB at 100Hz, 1kHz and 10kHz, taken from the Befaco Hexmix it copies. The code sets a low shelf of ±20dB at 125Hz, a mid peak of ±12.5dB at 1200Hz and a high shelf of ±15dB at 1800Hz, and the master EQ ±10dB at 120Hz, ±7dB at 1300Hz and ±7dB at 1700Hz. The ranges and frequencies above are the code's.

lines: CV to trigger utility: each of four inputs fires a gate whenever its voltage has moved more than a set amount since the last time it was read
Sets the gap between readings of the inputs, 16 samples at the bottom and 4400 at the top, about 100ms at 44.1kHz, so turning it up reads less often; it sets no pulse width, despite the tooltip name
Sets how big a move fires a gate, 0V to 2V of change between one reading and the next; at the bottom any change at all fires one
A voltage compared against its value at the previous reading, firing a gate at the matching output when it has moved more than the sensitivity allows
A 10V gate 10ms long, fired whenever the matching input has moved more than the sensitivity allows
retrig.notes: The panel prints sample rate on the large knob and the maker's tooltip names it pulse width; the code uses it as a frame counter setting the interval between comparisons, and the output pulse is fixed at 10ms.
